slice.question: Can logically identical candidate objects be forced to one canonical byte string/key, or explicitly rejected, across key order, Unicode normalization, numeric lexical encodings, and omitted/default fields?
slice.candidate: Schema-aware semantic canonicalization before immutable-key creation: reject duplicate raw keys and post-NFC key collisions; normalize strings/keys to NFC; materialize schema defaults; parse numeric JSON tokens into an exact decimal domain and emit a unique decimal spelling; sort object keys; emit whitespace-free UTF-8 JSON; derive the immutable candidate key from the canonical bytes.

public_basis.evidence: Provides deterministic JSON serialization rules but explicitly preserves Unicode strings as-is and does not perform Unicode normalization; bare JCS is therefore insufficient when NFC/NFD are intended to be semantically identical.

public_basis.source: Unicode Standard Annex #15, Unicode Normalization Forms
public_basis.evidence: NFC maps canonically equivalent strings to a unique normalized representation suitable for binary equality.

deterministic_test.harness: local finite state-free canonicalizer using exact Decimal parsing, NFC normalization, schema default insertion, sorted minimal JSON emission, and SHA-256 only as a diagnostic key
equivalence_cases: Unicode NFC café vs NFD cafe+U+0301
defaults mode=safe,retry=0 omitted vs explicitly present
deterministic_test.equivalence_result: PASS: all tested logically equivalent variants emitted the exact same canonical bytes and diagnostic key.

negative_controls.case: two distinct raw keys collapse to same NFC key

negative_controls.result: ACCEPT as semantically distinct types with different canonical bytes/key

slice.revision: Do not use bare JCS as the semantic-dedup key when Unicode canonical equivalence is intended. Use a schema-aware pre-canonicalization layer or a strict reject-only canonical-input profile before deterministic immutable-key creation.
slice.scope: Finite deterministic JSON-object cases only. Arbitrary Unicode, arbitrary-precision numeric schema semantics, arrays/large nested objects, and live repository race interleavings are not proven. SHA-256 was diagnostic in the test, not established as a required zero-dependency runtime primitive.
alternatives_preserved: Strict reject-only profile: accept only already-NFC, schema-complete, canonical-number inputs and reject all noncanonical variants instead of transforming them.
Concurrent create-conflict reconciliation after deterministic-key absence remains the next independent leaf.

phase1_constraints.qualification: This slice tests the serialization rule itself; operational correctness of arbitrary Unicode/decimal normalization inside scheduled Chat remains outside tested scope and is not claimed.

conflict_check: Frozen sanitized DESIRED_STATE control26/config8, own r177 LATEST, public RFC/Unicode sources, and a local deterministic test only; no O/O-derived, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger or scheduler semantics consumed.
frontier: Test concurrent write interleavings between read-at-K absence and create, including create-conflict reconciliation without in-run retry loops.
Later test whether a strict reject-only canonical-input profile is easier to make end-to-end zero-dependency than transform-and-normalize for arbitrary Unicode/decimal domains.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, bootstrap and freeze authority, then execute exactly one concurrent-write-interleaving leaf: model two writers that both read deterministic K absent, require at most one create attempt per writer, treat create conflict/ambiguous result as a bounded stop with next-invocation read-at-K reconciliation, and prove no overwrite plus stale-parent pointer CAS rejection. Preserve the strict reject-only canonical-input alternative for a later leaf.
